items.title: Eurreal Wilford "Little Brother" Montgomery Interview, 1958-05-29
items.q: Well it's King Oliver's numbers, he wrote it, yeah. ... So I'd taken it up on myself, I learned it off of the orchestration, you know.

ctx.x: Yeah, Oliver made a record of it.

Well it's King Oliver's numbers, he wrote it, yeah. So well he had it kind of complicated for musicians at the time, of course today it wouldn't be too much from the play, it wouldn't be nothing because they're more experienced, you know, in the reading abilities anyway. So that's what made it hard. It took a pretty good reader, sight reader to read it, played good. So I'd taken it up on myself, I learned it off of the orchestration, you know.
Are there any pianists that you might say influenced your style after you got more experience that you listened to and you say you picked it up mostly yourself and your brothers and sisters?

items.title: Eurreal Wilford "Little Brother" Montgomery Interview, 1958-05-29
items.q: Well at the time Lewis had left too, him and Joe Oliver who came up.

ctx.x: Well Lee Collins, he was good too. Lewis, he was good. Well at the time Lewis had left too, him and Joe Oliver who came up.
Yeah. Yeah. Did you hear any of the street bands, the parades? Oh yeah.
